sources.entry: Detect The Salient Features in an Image

summary.title: OpenCV Saliency Detection - PyImageSearch
summary.one_liner: You learn how to find the most visually prominent regions of an image in Python using OpenCV's contrib saliency module, covering static, objectness, and motion saliency.
keywords: detect what stands out in a photo
takeaways: Saliency detection locates the regions of an image that stand out; it is not object detection by itself.
OpenCV's saliency module (in opencv-contrib) offers static (spectral residual, fine grained), objectness (BING), and motion (Wang and Dudek 2014) detectors via cv2.saliency constructors.
Each detector's computeSaliency method returns a success flag and a saliency map, which is scaled to 0-255 for display or thresholded for contour extraction.
Motion saliency needs OpenCV 3.4 or newer; the author found it did not work on 3.3.
summary.summary: This PyImageSearch tutorial explains saliency detection, the automatic localisation of the most prominent parts of an image, and shows how to apply it with OpenCV's contrib saliency module in Python. It covers three classes of saliency: static, motion, and objectness, and walks through example scripts for each using images of soccer players, a boat, and a webcam feed. The author notes that OpenCV must be built with contrib and that the BING objectness detector needs nine small model files. The post is a hands-on code walkthrough with sample outputs.
